scope: One existing, functional Android app, one release/version, and one production submission to Google Play through the client account.

Version code/name and release configuration, a signed Android App Bundle (AAB), and coordination of the correct existing or new-app upload-key and Play App Signing setup. Preserve the existing application ID and signing identity for updates.

requirements.text: Share your Android repository, framework, working build instructions, application ID, and target release version. Confirm the app runs and builds. Include any prior Play review feedback and current SDK/build warnings.

Invite access to your verified Play Console account. Confirm production access is granted for this app and any required closed testing is complete. Enrollment, verification, tester recruitment, and production-access applications are separate.

Describe the existing Play App Signing and upload-key setup, or confirm this is a new app. Confirm the required signing access is available. Do not paste private keys or keystore passwords here; we will arrange secure access.

Provide final English listing text, icon, store-ready screenshots, feature graphic if required, support/privacy URLs, category, and release countries. Confirm you own or have rights to the app and all supplied materials.

Provide reviewer test access, up to 3 core flows to check, and confirmed Data safety/content-rating answers. Describe SDKs, data collection, ads, permissions, login, payments, and account deletion. Supply any other required app declarations.

summary:
Get your existing Android app prepared and submitted to Google Play through your own developer account.

One app, one release, one English listing.

Included:
- Release versioning, signing, and Android App Bundle preparation
- Checks of up to 3 agreed core flows
- Listing setup using your supplied text and store artwork
- Data safety and app-content entries from your confirmed answers
- Production release submission for review
- Configuration changes, submission confirmation, and handoff notes
- One metadata/signing revision and resubmission requested within 30 days

I built and released Agentic and SolPulse across web and mobile and have handled their release workflows.

Your Android app must already work and build. Your account must be verified with production access for this app; any required closed testing must be complete. You supply assets, access, and disclosures and pay account fees.

The 7-day scope is initial submission after prerequisites are ready. Google controls review and publication timing. Tester recruitment, app repairs, SDK migrations, and account appeals are separate.

Send your framework, build status, and production-access status before ordering.

faqs.q: Can a new personal Play account use this package?
faqs.a: Yes, after verification, any required closed testing, and production-access approval for the app are complete. Tester recruitment, managing closed tests, and applying for production access are separate from this submission package.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee approval or a publication date?
faqs.a: No. The deliverable is a signed release bundle and a production submission for review. Google controls approval and publication timing. The 7-day scope starts after the app, account eligibility, signing access, and assets are ready.

faqs.q: Do I need my own Google Play developer account?
faqs.a: Yes. You own the verified account, complete required agreements, grant invited Play Console access, and pay all fees. I use your account. Existing apps must have the appropriate upload/signing access available.

faqs.q: What happens if Google rejects the app?
faqs.a: One metadata/signing correction and resubmission requested within 30 days of initial submission is included. Product-code changes, policy-driven feature changes, SDK migrations, account appeals, and extra review rounds require separate scope.

Existing Kotlin or React Native Android apps that already work and build. Send build status and prior review feedback before ordering. App conversion, new features, store artwork, legal-document writing, and iOS submission are separate.
